holds.excerpt: Diagnose stored codes first: P1811 with harsh shifts points to the pressure control solenoid, which requires removing the transmission side cover (engine cradle lowered) to replace.
Test the crank sensor and ICM circuits and replace the failed component;
Test by swerving gently at 40-50 mph: noise quieter on right turn = left bearing bad.
Replace the melted bulb socket pigtail with a ceramic high-temperature H11 connector kit (14-gauge wire) and pack the new connector with dielectric grease.
Also scan wheel-speed and steering-position sensors before condemning the BCM.
Diagnose with a scan tool that reads body module roof codes — most repairs are weak hydraulic pumps ($400-800), leaking rams ($600-1200), or microswitch/latch sensor replacement ($150-400).
Toggling the hazard button often temporarily revives the signals, which confirms the diagnosis.
Diagnose low-retention, starting or cylinder complaints separately.
Diagnose separate switch/cylinder complaints independently.
For slipping or shudder, diagnose pressure and solenoid operation first;
Test for power at the blower connector: power present but no fan means a bad motor;
campaign applicability, diagnostic state, part number, programming and VIN fitment must be verified first.
Diagnose fuel-rail pressure and replace the high-pressure fuel pump;
First rule out a loose or worn gas cap, then test the vent VSV and replace it if stuck (a much cheaper repair than the full canister);
